 MMBets Game of the Week: The Dallas Mavericks look to course-correct against the reeling Golden State Warriors
 Dallas looks to take advantage of a Splash-Bro-less Warriors team
 by David Trink Nov 18, 2026, 8:08 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Mavericks face the Golden State Warriors at home on Wednesday night. It will be the first meeting between former Michigan teammates Morez Johnson Jr. and Yaxel Lendeborg, but the story will be about both of these teams righting the ship. The Warriors have dropped their last two games without Stephen Curry and did not eclipse 100 points in either contest. The Mavericks have lost three in a row in embarrassing fashion and have to get back on track against a bad Warriors team. It should be a “get right” game for Dallas, if they can muster any effort at all.

 How to watch: The local broadcast will be handled by KFAA Channel 29, with the game also airing on sister stations throughout the Mavs’ regional viewership area. You can catch the stream on MavsTV or on NBA League Pass where available. The radio broadcast is on KRLD 105.3 The Fan.
 Game Lines

 Spread Mavericks -4.5 (-110)
 Total O/U 225.5 (-106/-114)
 Moneyline Mavericks -198
 Tyler’s Plays 
 Over 225.5 points (-106) 
 Yaxel Lendeborg under 23.5 points (-114) 
 Al Horford under 6.5 points (+100) 
 Mavericks -9.5 (+172) 
 The Mavs have been obliterated defensively as of late and the warriors have been equally bad. Expect offensive fireworks in this one, but not from Yaxel Lendeborg or Al Horford. If there’s anyone who knows how to defend Yaxel, it’s his former coach Dusty May. And with Horford, I just can’t pass up this number. Lastly, as my associate David Trink said today, “My God the Warriors have gotten obliterated without Steph.” The Mavs get right in a big way at home.
 David’s Plays 
 Mavericks -4.5 (-110) 
 Kyrie Irving over 22.5 points (-114) 
 Cooper Flagg to score 30+ points (+310) 
 Mavericks over 114.5 points (-114) 
 Dallas is going to destroy this Golden State team. They have to show up, and I expect them to. It will be a top-down effort, with Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg taking advantage of the Warriors’ lack of a paint presence and leading Dallas to a rout, 121-102.
